questions.question: Which company's advertising fixed the modern image of the plump, jolly Santa from 1931 onwards?
questions.fun_fact: The red suit predates the campaign — illustrator Haddon Sundblom standardised the look rather than inventing it.

questions.question: Who commissioned Rudolph the reindeer in 1939?
questions.fun_fact: Robert L. May wrote the rhyming story as a giveaway booklet for the Montgomery Ward chain.

questions.question: Why has the North American air-defence command NORAD tracked Santa every year since 1955?

answers.text: Because of a misprinted telephone number
Because two generals made a bet

questions.fun_fact: A store advertisement printed a command centre's number instead of the Santa hotline, and the duty officer played along.

questions.question: Which holiday was the song 'Jingle Bells' originally written for?
questions.fun_fact: James Lord Pierpont published it in 1857 as 'One Horse Open Sleigh' — a winter song with no Christmas content at all.

questions.question: Which song was the first ever broadcast to Earth from space?
questions.fun_fact: In December 1965 the Gemini 6 crew first reported an 'unidentified object', then produced a harmonica and sleigh bells.

questions.question: Which instrument accompanied the first performance of 'Silent Night'?
questions.fun_fact: Why the organ stayed silent is unclear; the story about mice in the bellows was invented much later.

questions.question: Which Christmas recording is regarded as the best-selling single of all time?
questions.fun_fact: Estimates run past 50 million copies sold; no other single comes close.

questions.question: How long did it take Wham!'s 'Last Christmas' to reach number one in the UK charts?

answers.text: It went straight to number one

questions.fun_fact: In 1984 the charity single 'Do They Know It's Christmas?' blocked the top spot; the song finally got there in early 2021.

questions.question: How long did Mariah Carey and Walter Afanasieff reportedly take to write 'All I Want for Christmas Is You'?

answers.text: About a quarter of an hour

questions.fun_fact: The two still tell the story differently; the only point they agree on is that it happened very fast.

questions.question: What is the poinsettia named after?
questions.fun_fact: Joel Roberts Poinsett sent the plant home from Mexico to the United States in the 1820s.

questions.question: Which statement about the poinsettia as a houseplant is true?

answers.text: It is not deadly poisonous to humans
One leaf can kill a child
Its sap is a powerful nerve poison

questions.fun_fact: The milky sap irritates skin and stomach and nothing more; the killer reputation traces back to one unverified case from 1919.

questions.question: How does mistletoe feed itself?

answers.text: It taps its host tree and also photosynthesises

questions.fun_fact: As a hemiparasite it draws water and minerals from the tree but makes its own sugar.

questions.question: Why is there a good case that the reindeer pulling the sleigh are female?

answers.text: Males shed their antlers before winter

questions.fun_fact: Female reindeer keep their antlers into spring, so in December almost the only reindeer wearing antlers are cows.

questions.question: What happens to reindeer eyes in the Arctic winter?

answers.text: The reflective layer behind the retina turns from gold to blue

questions.fun_fact: The blue version scatters more light inside the eye, making the animals more sensitive during the polar night.

questions.question: Where does the big Christmas tree on London's Trafalgar Square come from?

answers.text: It is an annual gift from Oslo
It is grown on a plantation in Wales
It is auctioned off anew each year

questions.fun_fact: Norway has sent one every year since 1947 as thanks for British support during the Second World War.

questions.question: Who had the first commercial Christmas card printed in 1843?
questions.fun_fact: Cole simply had too much correspondence, so he printed a thousand cards and sold them at a shilling each.

questions.question: How long did Charles Dickens take to write 'A Christmas Carol'?
questions.fun_fact: He wrote it in 1843 while short of money and published it at his own expense; it sold out within days.

questions.question: What happened to Christmas in England under Oliver Cromwell?

answers.text: It was raised to a state holiday

questions.fun_fact: In 1647 the Puritans abolished it as unbiblical, and several towns rioted in response.

questions.question: When did Christmas become a federal public holiday in the United States?
questions.fun_fact: Until then 25 December was an ordinary working day in several states.

questions.question: Who invented the Advent wreath in 1839?

answers.text: The Hamburg educator Johann Hinrich Wichern

questions.fun_fact: Wichern hung a cartwheel of candles in his children's home so the children could count down the wait.

questions.question: In which country was the printed Advent calendar invented?
questions.fun_fact: Gerhard Lang sold the first printed cut-out sheets around 1904; the little doors came later.

questions.question: What does the X in 'Xmas' stand for?
questions.fun_fact: Chi is the first letter of Christós; the abbreviation is centuries old rather than a modern shortcut.

questions.question: How did Christmas Island in the Indian Ocean get its name?

answers.text: A captain passed it on Christmas Day 1643
A nativity scene was found there
It is shaped like a star

questions.fun_fact: William Mynors sailed by and simply entered the date as the name.

questions.question: Which meal counts as the classic Christmas dinner in Japan?

answers.text: Fried chicken from a fast-food chain

questions.fun_fact: A 1974 advertising campaign built around the slogan 'Kentucky for Christmas' hardened into a tradition.

questions.question: What is the typical Christmas cake in Japan?

answers.text: A sponge cake with cream and strawberries

questions.fun_fact: Red and white like the national colours; the cake sells on 24 December and almost nowhere after that.

questions.question: What do millions of Swedes traditionally watch at 3 p.m. on 24 December?
questions.fun_fact: 'Kalle Anka' has run almost unchanged since 1959, and attempts to move it have caused public outrage.

questions.question: What is put up on the main square of Gävle, Sweden, every Advent?

answers.text: A giant goat made of straw
A polar bear carved from ice

questions.fun_fact: The goat has been erected since 1966 and has been set on fire dozens of times.

questions.question: What do Norwegians traditionally hide on Christmas Eve?
questions.fun_fact: Old belief held that witches are abroad that night looking for something to ride.

questions.question: How many Yule Lads visit Icelandic children in the nights before Christmas?
questions.fun_fact: Each has his own quirk: one steals skyr, one licks spoons, one slams doors.

questions.question: What does the Icelandic 'Jólabókaflóð' refer to?

answers.text: The flood of books before Christmas

questions.fun_fact: Books are the classic gift, and the evening of the 24th belongs to reading with chocolate.

questions.question: What is the Catalan 'Caga Tió'?

answers.text: A nativity figure with a lantern

questions.fun_fact: Children feed the painted log for weeks, then beat it with sticks on 24 December until sweets fall out.

questions.question: Which figure traditionally belongs in a corner of a Catalan nativity scene?

answers.text: A crouching man with his trousers down

questions.fun_fact: The 'Caganer' symbolically fertilises the soil and is considered a good omen for the coming year.

questions.question: Which Christmas tree decoration is considered lucky in Ukraine?
questions.fun_fact: A legend tells of a poor widow whose bare tree was decorated overnight by spiders.

questions.question: How do many worshippers in Caracas get to early Mass on Christmas morning?
questions.fun_fact: Some neighbourhoods close streets to traffic for the 'Misa de Aguinaldo'.

questions.question: Which frightening figure accompanies St Nicholas in the Alpine countries?
questions.fun_fact: On 5 December whole Krampus runs move through Alpine towns in fur, horns and cowbells.

questions.question: From which country does the Dutch Sinterklaas arrive by steamboat each year, according to tradition?
questions.fun_fact: His November arrival is broadcast live across the country, and he brings presents on 5 December.

questions.question: What has been proclaimed in Turku, Finland, at noon on 24 December since the Middle Ages?

answers.text: The end of the fishing season

questions.fun_fact: The reading is broadcast on radio and counts as one of the country's oldest unbroken traditions.

questions.question: Where, according to Finnish tradition, is Santa's workshop?

answers.text: On the Korvatunturi fell in Lapland

questions.fun_fact: The fell is shaped like a pair of ears, which is how Santa is said to hear every child's wish.

questions.question: Which postal code has Canada Post assigned to Santa Claus?
questions.fun_fact: Volunteers answer millions of letters every year, each in the language the child wrote in.

questions.question: In which region did the historical bishop Nicholas, the origin of St Nicholas Day, actually live?
questions.fun_fact: His bones were taken to Bari in 1087 and remain there today.

questions.question: Who promoted the Christ Child as the gift-bringer in German-speaking countries?
questions.fun_fact: Luther wanted to push back the cult of saints; ironically it was Catholic regions that later held on to the Christkind longest.

questions.question: Who plays the Nuremberg Christkind at the city's Christmas market?

answers.text: A young woman elected every two years
A child from the cathedral school

questions.fun_fact: Applicants must live in Nuremberg, be at least 1.60 metres tall and have a head for heights.

questions.question: Since when is Dresden's Striezelmarkt documented?
questions.fun_fact: It began as a one-day meat market before the feast, which makes it one of the oldest Christmas markets anywhere.

questions.question: Which German region produces the classic nutcracker and incense-smoker figures?
questions.fun_fact: When mining declined whole villages lived from carving, which is why the nutcracker so often wears a uniform.

questions.question: How was Tchaikovsky's ballet 'The Nutcracker' received at its 1892 premiere?

answers.text: It was abandoned after the first act

questions.fun_fact: Critics found the plot thin and the children's roles odd; it only became a Christmas fixture decades later.

questions.question: How many parts does Johann Sebastian Bach's Christmas Oratorio have?
questions.fun_fact: The parts were written for six separate services between 25 December 1734 and 6 January 1735.

questions.question: At which time of year was Handel's 'Messiah' first performed?
questions.fun_fact: The premiere was in Dublin in April 1742; only later did the work drift into the Christmas season.

questions.question: What happened along parts of the Western Front at Christmas 1914?

answers.text: Soldiers from both sides left the trenches and celebrated together
The war was officially suspended for two days

questions.fun_fact: There was singing, cigarettes and in places football; high commands forbade any repeat in later years.

questions.question: Who put up the first electrically lit Christmas tree in 1882?
questions.fun_fact: Edward H. Johnson had 80 red, white and blue bulbs hand-wired and set the tree rotating as well.

questions.question: What was tinsel originally made of?
questions.fun_fact: Nuremberg craftsmen were beating it from around 1610; it tarnished over time and had to be replaced.

questions.question: Where did the making of glass Christmas baubles begin?
questions.fun_fact: Legend says a glassblower could not afford apples and nuts for his tree, so he blew himself some out of glass.

questions.question: What did English mince pies originally contain?
questions.fun_fact: Minced meat, suet and dried fruit together were a preserving trick; the meat only vanished in the 19th century.

questions.question: What is the British 'Stir-up Sunday'?

answers.text: The Sunday the Christmas pudding is mixed

questions.fun_fact: Every family member stirs once, clockwise, and makes a wish while doing it.

questions.question: Which drink outsells cola in Sweden at Christmas?
questions.fun_fact: The dark malt drink shifts December market shares so hard that Coca-Cola at times produced a version itself.

questions.question: Which continent does the turkey, now the Christmas roast in many countries, come from?
questions.fun_fact: Before it was brought over in the 16th century, Europe's festive roasts were goose, pork or peacock.

questions.question: What is one of the most common Christmas Eve dinners in Germany?
questions.fun_fact: The classic has a practical reason: it can be prepared in the morning and does not tie up the evening.

questions.question: What was the British 'Boxing Day' on 26 December originally?

answers.text: The day servants and the poor received their gift box
The day presents are exchanged in shops

questions.fun_fact: The name comes from alms boxes and parcels, not from the sport and not from unwrapping.

questions.question: When do the 'Twelve Days of Christmas' of the song actually run?
questions.fun_fact: They end on the eve of Epiphany, so the song counts away from Christmas rather than towards it.

questions.question: What does the German word 'Weihnachten' go back to?
questions.fun_fact: The Middle High German phrase 'ze den wîhen nahten' means the hallowed nights around the feast.

questions.question: Where does the red-and-green colour pairing of Christmas come from?

answers.text: From holly, with red berries against green leaves
From the flag of the Papal States

questions.fun_fact: Evergreens bearing red fruit stood for life in winter long before Christianity.

questions.question: What was the original Yule log?

answers.text: A large log meant to burn through the holidays
A cake shaped like a tree trunk

questions.fun_fact: Only when open hearths grew rare did the motif move onto the cake plate; the French bûche de Noël is a replica.

questions.question: How did the 1946 film 'It's a Wonderful Life' become the classic it is?

answers.text: Its copyright lapsed and stations aired it for free
It became required viewing in schools

questions.fun_fact: It lost money at the box office; the endless 1970s television repeats made it a fixture.

questions.question: In which city is most of 'Home Alone' set?
questions.fun_fact: The family flies to Paris while Kevin stays behind in suburban Chicago; filming was in Winnetka, Illinois.

questions.question: Why do many people count 'Die Hard' as a Christmas film?

answers.text: It takes place at a Christmas party on 24 December
The hero's middle name is Nicholas

questions.fun_fact: The argument is as old as it is stubborn, and the director and the lead actor have publicly disagreed about it.

questions.question: Who wrote the jazz score for the 1965 television classic 'A Charlie Brown Christmas'?
questions.fun_fact: The network first thought a jazz trio was wrong for a children's show; the record went on to sell millions.

questions.question: Who turned 'Rudolph, the Red-Nosed Reindeer' into a worldwide hit song in 1949?
questions.fun_fact: Autry hesitated for a long time and only recorded it because his wife pushed him; it became his best-selling record.

questions.question: In which text did Santa's eight reindeer first appear by name?
questions.fun_fact: 'A Visit from St. Nicholas' also named Donder and Blitzen, which are Dutch for thunder and lightning.

questions.question: In which country was the charity Christmas seal invented in 1904?
questions.fun_fact: A postal clerk proposed the extra stamp to fund children's hospitals, and the idea spread worldwide.

questions.question: Which legend explains the hung-up Christmas stockings?

answers.text: Nicholas threw gold through a window and it landed in stockings
A tailor lost his stocking up a chimney
Miners dried their stockings by the fire

questions.fun_fact: In the story the gold saved the three daughters of a ruined man from destitution.

questions.question: What is true about the 'German tradition' of the Christmas pickle on the tree?

answers.text: Hardly anyone in Germany has heard of it
It was invented in Bavaria in 1850

questions.fun_fact: The custom is mainly American and was marketed there with an invented German origin story.

questions.question: Where did the custom of kissing under mistletoe arise?
questions.fun_fact: The 18th-century rule was that each kiss cost a berry, and when the sprig was bare the kissing stopped.

questions.question: What happens to the wood of the big Rockefeller Center tree after the holidays?

answers.text: It is milled into lumber for charity housing

questions.fun_fact: Since 2007 the boards go to Habitat for Humanity; a tree has stood there almost every year since 1931.

questions.question: What rank did the 'Good King Wenceslas' of the carol actually hold?

answers.text: He was a duke of Bohemia
He was a king of Poland

questions.fun_fact: Wenceslas I was only granted royal title posthumously; the carol promotes him in advance.

questions.question: Where does the melody of 'O Christmas Tree' come from?
questions.fun_fact: Ernst Anschütz wrote today's words in 1824 to a long-known tune that had previously been about an unfaithful lover.

questions.question: Which honour did 'Silent Night' receive from UNESCO in 2011?

answers.text: It became Austrian intangible cultural heritage
It joined the Memory of the World register
It was declared a world anthem

questions.fun_fact: The song has been translated into well over 300 languages and dialects.

questions.question: What does the Latin word 'adventus', the root of Advent, mean?
questions.fun_fact: Advent was originally a fasting period, which is why the food before 24 December used to be plain.

questions.question: What traditionally goes under the tablecloth at the Polish 'Wigilia'?
questions.fun_fact: It recalls the manger, and one place at the table is also left free for an unexpected guest.

questions.question: What are the Greek 'kallikantzaroi'?

answers.text: Goblins who make mischief between Christmas and Epiphany

questions.fun_fact: Legend says they saw at the world tree all year and only surface during the twelve nights.

questions.question: On which day is Christmas ('Genna') celebrated in Ethiopia?
questions.fun_fact: The Ethiopian Orthodox Church follows its own calendar, and the Ethiopian year runs behind the Gregorian one.

questions.question: How many evenings do the Mexican 'posadas' before Christmas last?
questions.fun_fact: They re-enact the search for shelter; each evening ends at a different front door with singing and a piñata.

questions.question: What do the seven points of the classic Mexican Christmas piñata stand for?

answers.text: The seven days of the week

questions.fun_fact: Striking it blindfolded means striking blindly at sin, and the sweets are the reward of faith.

questions.question: Who draws the numbers of Spain's 'El Gordo' Christmas lottery and sings out the prizes?

answers.text: Notaries of the Bank of Spain

questions.fun_fact: Children of the San Ildefonso school have sung number and amount in alternation since the 18th century.

questions.question: Who traditionally brings children their presents in Spain?
questions.fun_fact: On the night before 6 January children put out shoes and some water for the camels.

questions.question: Which country is known for the longest Christmas season in the world?
questions.fun_fact: As soon as September starts the carols come on, and the season runs into January.

questions.question: What shape is the Filipino Christmas lantern, the 'parol'?
questions.fun_fact: It stands for the star of Bethlehem and was originally built from bamboo and rice paper.

questions.question: In which season does Australia celebrate Christmas?
questions.fun_fact: Barbecues on the beach and open-air 'Carols by Candlelight' are part of the day there.

questions.question: Why do Russian Orthodox believers celebrate Christmas on 7 January?

answers.text: Because the church keeps the Julian calendar
Because a tsar moved the date
Because 25 December is a working day

questions.fun_fact: The gap to the Gregorian calendar currently stands at thirteen days.

questions.question: What does the recipe rule for Nuremberg Elisenlebkuchen require?

answers.text: No more than ten per cent flour

questions.fun_fact: The protected designation also demands a high proportion of nuts, which is why they stay so moist.

questions.question: What is the shape of the Dresden Christstollen meant to represent?

answers.text: The Christ child wrapped in swaddling cloth

questions.fun_fact: The icing sugar stands for the cloths; the recipe was long limited by the Advent ban on butter.

questions.question: Which city is panettone from?
questions.fun_fact: With its starter and several rises the dough often takes more than 30 hours.

questions.question: How far back is spiced hot wine documented in Europe?
questions.fun_fact: A Roman cookbook describes 'conditum paradoxum' of wine, honey and pepper — the ancestor of mulled wine.

questions.question: In which city is the decorated Christmas tree first documented?
questions.fun_fact: A 1539 guild record mentions a tree in the cathedral; candles came much later.

questions.question: Since when has the British royal Christmas message existed?
questions.fun_fact: George V spoke on radio first; the first televised message followed only in 1957.

questions.question: What is notable about José Feliciano's 1970 'Feliz Navidad'?

answers.text: The lyric is just a few lines in Spanish and English
It is the longest charting Christmas song

questions.fun_fact: Feliciano needed only minutes for the words and played the cuatro on the track.

questions.question: Which astronomical explanation did Johannes Kepler propose for the star of Bethlehem?

answers.text: A close conjunction of Jupiter and Saturn

questions.fun_fact: Kepler watched such a conjunction in 1603 and calculated back to the year 7 BCE.

questions.question: What does the Bible say about the date of Jesus's birth?

answers.text: It gives no date at all

questions.fun_fact: 25 December took hold in the 4th century and coincided with Roman festivals around the winter solstice.

questions.question: How many gifts do you receive in total if every day of 'The Twelve Days of Christmas' repeats all the earlier ones?
questions.fun_fact: 364 — almost one for every day of the year, including twelve partridges in a pear tree.

questions.question: In which year was 'Silent Night' sung for the first time?
questions.fun_fact: 1818, in Oberndorf near Salzburg, accompanied on a guitar rather than the organ.

questions.question: How tall is the Gävle straw goat that goes up every Advent in Sweden?
questions.fun_fact: 13 metres tall and about 3.6 tonnes; even so it has often failed to survive Advent.

questions.question: How many reindeer are named in the 1823 poem 'A Visit from St. Nicholas'?
questions.fun_fact: Eight; Rudolph was added 116 years later as an advertising invention.

questions.question: How many doors does a classic Advent calendar have?
questions.fun_fact: 24 — the calendar ends on Christmas Eve rather than on Christmas Day.
